s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent paroxysmal chest pain
salient_findings: Paroxysmal chest pain occurring 5 times during the day
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR on initial ECG
key_facts: Patient presented to the emergency department with chest pain
Chest pain was paroxysmal and occurred 5 times during the day
Each episode of chest pain lasted 15 to 30 minutes
Blood pressure was 106/52 mm Hg
Pulse rate was 64 beats per minute
Chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds with no murmurs
Hemogram, serum electrolyte levels, kidney and liver function tests, B-type natriuretic peptide and D-dimer levels were all within normal limits
Cardiac troponin I level was elevated at 25 ng/mL
Initial ECG revealed sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
Repeated ECG revealed sinus bradycardia, Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
Coronary angiography showed total occlusion of the right coronary artery and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and total occlusion of the right coronary artery

shortlist.label: Unstable angina
shortlist.why_kept: Paroxysmal chest pain and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery

shortlist.label: Variant angina
shortlist.why_kept: ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, and recurrent chest pain

shortlist.label: Coronary artery dissection
shortlist.why_kept: Total occlusion of the right coronary artery and clinical presentation of acute coronary syndrome

shortlist.label: Prinzmetal's angina
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent paroxysmal chest pain and ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR

raw.rationale: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and ECG changes including ST-segment elevation and Q-wave formation are indicative of myocardial infarction

rejected.label: Unstable angina
rejected.why: Unstable angina typically does not present with elevated troponin levels or Q-wave formation on ECG

rejected.label: Variant angina
rejected.why: Variant angina (Prinzmetal's angina) is characterized by transient ST-segment elevation during episodes of chest pain, but does not typically result in elevated troponin levels or Q-wave formation

rejected.label: Coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: While coronary artery dissection can cause myocardial infarction, the provided information does not specifically suggest dissection as the primary cause

rejected.label: Prinzmetal's angina
rejected.why: Prinzmetal's angina is another term for variant angina, which does not fit with the elevated troponin and Q-wave formation seen in this case
